The A1+2c and A1+2a+b were divided en bloc via stapling, followed by the stapled division of the B1+2 (after frozen-section confirmation of negative peribronchial nodes). V1+2 was divided with clips. Intersegmental plane delineation was performed using IV-ICG, with stapled parenchymal division ensuring adequate margins. Operative time 2:17 (console time 1:32), minimal blood loss, chest tube out POD1, discharged POD5.

literature.headline_zh: 人偏肺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 两种 疫苗 构建体都表现出高抗原性,同时保持无毒和非过敏性,具有良好的理化特性;结构分析表明 疫苗 模型的构象稳定,分子对接研究表明与 TLR2 和 TLR4 具有很强的结合亲和力。 [10.1007/s44368-026-00027-w]
几种植物化学物质显示出有希望的对接结果,并有助于 HMPV F 蛋白的结构稳定,特别是在其对膜融合至关重要的七肽重复区域和融合环区域。 [10.1007/s40203-026-00716-2]
三种 siRNA 候选物(F11、F19 和 F26)表现出良好的 RNAi 特性,其中 F11 表现出最高的序列保守性、解链温度、AGO2 相互作用和稳定的动态行为。 [10.1016/j.jgeb.2026.100783]

人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 是一种新发现的常见呼吸道病毒,于 2001 年首次发现。HMPV 是婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下个体中上呼吸道感染和 下呼吸道感染 的主要原因。尽管它已广泛传播多年,但 HMPV 经常未被诊断,也没有获得许可的 疫苗 或特定的 抗病毒药物 治疗。该病毒主要通过以下途径传播:呼吸道飞沫、直接接触和受污染的表面,高峰出现在冬末和春季。几乎所有儿童在五岁时都会接触 HMPV,他们一生中都可能经历再次感染。HMPV 发病机制 涉及病毒蛋白和 宿主 免疫之间复杂的相互作用。该病毒削弱先天 免疫应答,抑制干扰素信号传导,并促进 Th2 偏向的炎症反应。这会导致气道炎症、粘液分泌过多,严重时会导致细支气管炎或肺炎。T细胞功能障碍和免疫逃避策略导致感染时间延长,疾病严重程度增加。目前的治疗主要依靠支持性护理。利巴韦林、靶向融合(F)蛋白的单克隆抗体和基于肽的融合抑制剂已在实验研究中显示出潜力,但临床证据有限。努力开发疫苗,包括灭活、亚基和基于F蛋白的方法最有希望。在有效的疫苗或靶向治疗出现之前,手部卫生、呼吸礼仪、环境消毒和医疗机构感染控制等预防策略也至关重要。持续研究对于减轻HMPV感染的全球临床和经济负担至关重要。 [10.58257/ijprems54418]

Distinct index cases occurred in 236 (23%) households for HMPV, with a secondary attack rate of 8.7% and a median generation time of 7 days. [10.64898/2026.08.02.26359491]. papers.title: In silico docking and molecular dynamics simulation analysis of phytochemicals targeting human metapneumovirus fusion protein.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) continues to be a major cause of respiratory infections around the world, despite the availability of many treatment options and the existence of effective vaccines against other respiratory viruses such as influenza and parainfluenza virus. Since the virus poses a significant public health threat, yet there are no approved antiviral medications or vaccines against it, an effective therapy is still needed. This work aimed to find natural phytochemical inhibitors for HMPV fusion (F) glycoprotein by using a structure-based in silico drug discovery approach. As the protein has an important role in viral attachment to cells and membrane fusion, the choice of HMPV F glycoprotein as a drug target seemed to be appropriate. Compounds from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) 2.0 database were screened by performing molecular docking analysis of their interactions and binding affinities towards the HMPV F protein. The top-ranking molecules were further analyzed by conducting 300-nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations in order to obtain insights into complex stabilities, flexibilities, and conformations. Several phytochemicals showed promising docking results and contributed to structural stabilization of the target protein, especially its heptad repeat and fusion loops regions responsible for membrane fusion. These findings support their potential as fusion inhibitors and offer a promising foundation for future experimental validation and antiviral drug development. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes serious respiratory illness, yet no vaccines or antivirals exist. Using computer-based screening, we tested natural compounds from the IMPPAT 2.0 database against the virus's fusion (F) protein. Several phytochemicals showed stable binding, especially at key functional regions, suggesting they could block viral entry. These results highlight promising natural candidates for future HMPV drug development. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40203-026-00716-2.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) remains a major cause of respiratory infections globally, yet no approved antiviral medications or vaccines exist despite effective vaccines for other respiratory viruses such as influenza and parainfluenza virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a structure-based in silico drug discovery approach to identify natural phytochemical inhibitors targeting the HMPV fusion (F) glycoprotein.
analysis.methods: Compounds from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) 2.0 database were screened using molecular docking analysis to assess interactions and binding affinities with the HMPV F protein, followed by 300-nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate complex stability, flexibility, and conformation.
analysis.main_results: Several phytochemicals demonstrated promising docking results and contributed to structural stabilization of the HMPV F protein, particularly at its heptad repeat and fusion loops regions critical for membrane fusion.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings support the potential of these phytochemicals as fusion inhibitors and provide a foundation for future experimental validation and antiviral drug development against HMPV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies promising natural candidates for HMPV antiviral development, addressing the unmet need for effective therapies against this significant respiratory pathogen.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in silico predictions without experimental validation, which constrains the strength of conclusions regarding therapeutic efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This in silico study aimed to discover natural phytochemical inhibitors targeting the human metapneumovirus (HMPV) fusion (F) glycoprotein, motivated by the absence of approved antivirals or vaccines despite HMPV's global burden of respiratory disease. Using molecular docking and 300-ns molecular dynamics simulations, the authors screened compounds from the IMPPAT 2.0 database and identified several phytochemicals that stably bind key functional regions of the HMPV F protein, including heptad repeats and fusion loops essential for viral entry. These candidates showed potential to block membrane fusion and viral attachment, offering a promising foundation for future experimental validation. While the study provides computationally supported leads, the lack of in vitro or in vivo confirmation limits the strength of evidence and precludes clinical translation at this stage.

papers.title_zh: 针对 人偏肺病毒 融合蛋白的植物化学物质的计算机对接和分子动力学模拟分析。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) continues to be a major cause of respiratory infections around the world, despite the availability of many treatment options and the existence of effective vaccines against other respiratory viruses such as influenza and parainfluenza virus. Since the virus poses a significant public health threat, yet there are no approved antiviral medications or vaccines against it, an effective therapy is still needed. This work aimed to find natural phytochemical inhibitors for HMPV fusion (F) glycoprotein by using a structure-based in silico drug discovery approach. As the protein has an important role in viral attachment to cells and membrane fusion, the choice of HMPV F glycoprotein as a drug target seemed to be appropriate. Compounds from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) 2.0 database were screened by performing molecular docking analysis of their interactions and binding affinities towards the HMPV F protein. The top-ranking molecules were further analyzed by conducting 300-nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations in order to obtain insights into complex stabilities, flexibilities, and conformations. Several phytochemicals showed promising docking results and contributed to structural stabilization of the target protein, especially its heptad repeat and fusion loops regions responsible for membrane fusion. These findings support their potential as fusion inhibitors and offer a promising foundation for future experimental validation and antiviral drug development. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes serious respiratory illness, yet no vaccines or antivirals exist. Using computer-based screening, we tested natural compounds from the IMPPAT 2.0 database against the virus's fusion (F) protein. Several phytochemicals showed stable binding, especially at key functional regions, suggesting they could block viral entry. These results highlight promising natural candidates for future HMPV drug development. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40203-026-00716-2.

papers.title: Household Transmission of Human Metapneumovirus and Human Parainfluenza Viruses 1-4 in the United States, 2022-2024
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) and human parainfluenza viruses (HPIV 1-4) are common causes of seasonal respiratory illness, but their household transmission dynamics remain poorly defined. We analyzed weekly symptom data and nasal swabs from a prospective household surveillance study in Washington and Oregon from June 2022 to March 2024. Swabs were tested for HMPV and HPIV, and a subset underwent whole-genome sequencing. Distinct index cases occurred in 236 (23%) and 341 (36%) of 1,040 households for HMPV and HPIV, respectively. Household secondary attack rates (SAR) and median generation times were similar for HMPV (8.7%, 7 days) and HPIV (7.3%, 7 days). Sequenced samples reflected contemporaneous circulating strains during the same period, with household sequences clustering closely together. High-quality viral whole genome sequences were recovered for two or more individuals within a household in a total of 26 households for HMPV and 45 households for HPIV. Intra-household pairwise nucleotide (nt) distance ranged from 0 to 14 nt (median 0) for HMPV and 0-8 nt (median 1) for HPIV when cases occurred 0-15 days apart. Transmission occurred primarily from children to adults, emphasizing the importance of childcare- and school-associated spread and supporting child-focused prevention strategies to reduce household transmission.

papers.title: [Significance of the multi-pathogen surveillance of pediatric patients with acute respiratory infections in Beijing from 2024 to 2025].
papers.abstract: Objective: To delineate the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological features of acute respiratory infections (ARI) among pediatric patients in Beijing during 2024-2025. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 1 435 children diagnosed with ARI were enrolled from outpatient, emergency, respiratory medicine, and critical care medicine department of Capital Center for Children's Health, Capital Medical University between July 2024 and June 2025. Respiratory specimens were collected and screened for 28 respiratory pathogens using multiplex real-time quantitative PCR. Specimens positive for influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV), and human rhinovirus were further subtyped. Patients were categorized into influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) groups. Positivity rates across different sources, visit periods, and age groups were compared using the chi-square test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Results: Among the 1 435 children, there were 770 males and 665 females, with an age at presentation was 6.7 (4.4, 12.6) years. The total positive rate for the 28 pathogens was 80.5% (1 155/1 435). The ILI group comprised 1 040 cases (549 males, 491 females) with age at presentation was 6.8 (4.5, 12.8) years and the positive rate of 76.6% (797/1 040). Common viral pathogens included human rhinovirus 15.7% (163/1 040), human parainfluenza-virus (HPIV) 10.3% (107/1 040), and Influenza virus 7.1% (74/1 040), while common bacterial and atypical pathogens included Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) 18.7% (194/1 040), Haemophilus influenzae (HI) 18.4% (191/1 040), and Streptococcus pneumonia (SP) 17.1% (178/1 040). The SARI group comprised 395 cases (221 males, 174 females) with age at presentation was 6.5 (4.0, 12.3) years and the positive rate of 90.6% (358/395). Common viral pathogens included human rhinovirus 17.2% (68/395), RSV 9.9% (39/395), and HPIV 7.1% (28/395), while common bacterial and atypical pathogens included MP 51.4% (203/395), SP 15.4% (61/395), and HI 13.4% (53/395). Co-detections of multiple pathogens accounted for 43.0% (497/1 155) of all positive cases. The positivity rates of RSV and MP in the SARI group were significantly higher than those in the ILI group (both P<0.001). RSV positive rate was the highest in children under 1 year of age, accounting for 15.3% (13/85), while MP positive rate was the highest in children aged 7 to 18 years, accounting for 38.1% (205/538). Typing results revealed that 96.5% (83/86) were typed to H1N1 among influenza virus A cases, while 58.3% (42/72) were genotyped as RSV-A ON1 among RSV cases, 86.3% (63/73) were subtyped to B2 among HMPV cases, and 45.0% (104/231) were typed to human rhinovirus-A among human rhinovirus cases. Conclusion: The pathogen spectrum of pediatric patients with ARI in Beijing from 2024 to 2025 was characterized by the alternation or co-circulation of multiple bacteria and viruses, a high rate of co-detection of multiple pathogens, and different between SARI and ILI groups. Influenza virus was dominated by H1N1, RSV by RSV-A, HMPV by HMPV-B2, and human rhinovirus by human rhinovirus-A.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological features of acute respiratory infections (ARI) in 1,435 pediatric patients in Beijing from July 2024 to June 2025. Using multiplex real-time PCR, 28 respiratory pathogens were screened, with an overall positivity rate of 80.5%. Co-detections occurred in 43.0% of positive cases. Key findings included higher positivity rates of RSV and Mycoplasma pneumoniae in severe cases (SARI) compared to influenza-like illness (ILI). Subtyping revealed HMPV-B2 dominance (86.3%) among HMPV cases. The study highlights the co-circulation of multiple pathogens and age-specific distributions, informing targeted surveillance and interventions.

elements_zh.main_results: Among the 1 435 children, there were 770 males and 665 females, with an age at presentation was 6.7 (4.4, 12.6) years. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 2024-2025年北京市儿童急性呼吸道感染病原谱具有多种细菌和病毒交替或共循环、多种病原体共检出率高、SARI组和ILI组之间存在差异的特点。流感病毒以H1N1为主,RSV以RSV-A为主,HMPV以HMPV-B2为主,人鼻病毒以人鼻病毒A为主。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过识别主要病原体及其亚型(例如 HMPV-B2)为 监测 和预防策略提供信息,这可以指导儿科人群的有针对性的干预措施和公共卫生应对措施。

papers.title_zh: 2024-2025年北京市儿童急性呼吸道感染患者多病原监测的意义[J].
papers.source_body_en: Objective: To delineate the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological features of acute respiratory infections (ARI) among pediatric patients in Beijing during 2024-2025. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 1 435 children diagnosed with ARI were enrolled from outpatient, emergency, respiratory medicine, and critical care medicine department of Capital Center for Children's Health, Capital Medical University between July 2024 and June 2025. Respiratory specimens were collected and screened for 28 respiratory pathogens using multiplex real-time quantitative PCR. Specimens positive for influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV), and human rhinovirus were further subtyped. Patients were categorized into influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) groups. Positivity rates across different sources, visit periods, and age groups were compared using the chi-square test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Results: Among the 1 435 children, there were 770 males and 665 females, with an age at presentation was 6.7 (4.4, 12.6) years. The total positive rate for the 28 pathogens was 80.5% (1 155/1 435). The ILI group comprised 1 040 cases (549 males, 491 females) with age at presentation was 6.8 (4.5, 12.8) years and the positive rate of 76.6% (797/1 040). Common viral pathogens included human rhinovirus 15.7% (163/1 040), human parainfluenza-virus (HPIV) 10.3% (107/1 040), and Influenza virus 7.1% (74/1 040), while common bacterial and atypical pathogens included Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) 18.7% (194/1 040), Haemophilus influenzae (HI) 18.4% (191/1 040), and Streptococcus pneumonia (SP) 17.1% (178/1 040). The SARI group comprised 395 cases (221 males, 174 females) with age at presentation was 6.5 (4.0, 12.3) years and the positive rate of 90.6% (358/395). Common viral pathogens included human rhinovirus 17.2% (68/395), RSV 9.9% (39/395), and HPIV 7.1% (28/395), while common bacterial and atypical pathogens included MP 51.4% (203/395), SP 15.4% (61/395), and HI 13.4% (53/395). Co-detections of multiple pathogens accounted for 43.0% (497/1 155) of all positive cases. The positivity rates of RSV and MP in the SARI group were significantly higher than those in the ILI group (both P<0.001). RSV positive rate was the highest in children under 1 year of age, accounting for 15.3% (13/85), while MP positive rate was the highest in children aged 7 to 18 years, accounting for 38.1% (205/538). Typing results revealed that 96.5% (83/86) were typed to H1N1 among influenza virus A cases, while 58.3% (42/72) were genotyped as RSV-A ON1 among RSV cases, 86.3% (63/73) were subtyped to B2 among HMPV cases, and 45.0% (104/231) were typed to human rhinovirus-A among human rhinovirus cases. Conclusion: The pathogen spectrum of pediatric patients with ARI in Beijing from 2024 to 2025 was characterized by the alternation or co-circulation of multiple bacteria and viruses, a high rate of co-detection of multiple pathogens, and different between SARI and ILI groups. Influenza virus was dominated by H1N1, RSV by RSV-A, HMPV by HMPV-B2, and human rhinovirus by human rhinovirus-A.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 描绘2024-2025年北京市儿童急性呼吸道感染(ARI)的病原谱和流行病学特征。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本横断面研究纳入了2024年7月至2025年6月首都医科大学首都儿童健康中心门诊、急诊、呼吸内科和重症医学科1 435名确诊为ARI的儿童。
analysis_zh.methods: 收集呼吸道标本并使用多重实时定量 PCR 筛查 28 种呼吸道病原体。对流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、人偏肺病毒(HMPV)和人鼻病毒呈阳性的标本进行了进一步的亚型分析。使用卡方检验和 Wilcoxon 秩和检验比较不同来源、访问时间和年龄组的阳性率。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 2024-2025年北京市儿童急性呼吸道感染病原谱具有多种细菌和病毒交替或共循环、多种病原体共检出率高、SARI组和ILI组之间存在差异的特点。流感病毒以H1N1为主,RSV以RSV-A为主,HMPV以HMPV-B2为主,人鼻病毒以人鼻病毒A为主。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过识别主要病原体及其亚型(例如 HMPV-B2)为 监测 和预防策略提供信息,这可以指导儿科人群的有针对性的干预措施和公共卫生应对措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是横断面的,限制了因果推断。由于样本量大和病原体筛查全面,证据强度适中,但单中心设计可能限制普遍性。

papers.title: HUMAN METAPNEUMOVIRUS: EPIDEMIOLOGY, PATHOGENESIS, AND CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a newly identified common respiratory virus first discovered in 2001.HMPV is a leading cause of upper and lower respiratory tract infections in infants, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals.Even though it has circulated widely for years, HMPV is often not diagnosed and does not have a licensed vaccine or specific antiviral treatment.The virus mainly spreads through respiratory droplets, direct contact, and contaminated surfaces, with peaks occurring in late winter and spring.Almost all children are exposed to HMPV by the time they are five, and they may experience reinfections throughout their lives.HMPV pathogenesis involves complex interactions between viral proteins and host immunity.The virus weakens innate immune responses, suppresses interferon signaling, and promotes a Th2-skewed inflammatory response.This leads to airway inflammation, excess mucus production, and in severe cases, bronchiolitis or pneumonia.T-cell dysfunction and immune evasion strategies result in prolonged infection and increased disease severity.Current management relies mainly on supportive care.Ribavirin, monoclonal antibodies that target the fusion (F) protein, and peptide-based fusion inhibitors have shown potential in experimental studies, but there is limited clinical evidence.Efforts to develop vaccines, including inactivated, subunit, and live-attenuated candidates, are ongoing.Fprotein-based approaches show the most promise.Until effective vaccines or targeted therapies are available, prevention strategies such as hand hygiene, respiratory etiquette, environmental disinfection, and infection control in healthcare settings is also essential.Continued research is critical to reducing the global clinical and economic burden of HMPV infections.
papers.journal: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science

elements_en.main_results: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a newly identified common respiratory virus first discovered in 2001.HMPV is a leading cause of upper and lower respiratory tract infections in infants, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals.Even though it has circulated widely for years, HMPV is often not diagnosed and does not have a licensed vaccine or specific antiviral treatment.The virus mainly spreads through respiratory droplets, direct contact, and contaminated surfaces, with peaks occurring in late winter and spring.Almost all children are exposed to HMPV by the time they are five, and they may experience reinfections throughout their lives.HMPV pathogenesis involves complex interactions between viral proteins and host immunity.The virus weakens innate immune responses, suppresses interferon signaling, and promotes a Th2-skewed inflammatory response.This leads to airway inflammation, excess mucus production, and in severe cases, bronchiolitis or pneumonia.T-cell dysfunction and immune evasion strategies result in prolonged infection and increased disease severity.Current management relies mainly on supportive care.Ribavirin, monoclonal antibodies that target the fusion (F) protein, and peptide-based fusion inhibitors have shown potential in experimental studies, but there is limited clinical evidence.Efforts to develop vaccines, including inactivated, subunit, and live-attenuated candidates, are ongoing.Fprotein-based approaches show the most promise.Until effective vaccines or targeted therapies are available, prevention strategies such as hand hygiene, respiratory etiquette, environmental disinfection, and infection control in healthcare settings is also essential.Continued research is critical to reducing the global clinical and economic burden of HMPV infections.

papers.title: Harnessing reverse vaccinology for the design and validation of mRNA vaccine targeting the glycoprotein of human metapneumovirus (HMPV)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a major cause of respiratory illness among vulnerable populations worldwide, yet no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral therapy is currently available. This study aimed to design novel multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidates against HMPV using an immunoinformatics-based approach. Methods Globally representative HMPV glycoprotein sequences were analyzed to predict cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), helper T-lymphocyte (HTL), and linear B-cell (LBL) epitopes. Selected epitopes were assembled into two multi-epitope mRNA vaccine constructs. The constructs were further evaluated for antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, and physicochemical properties using in silico tools. Structural stability and immune receptor interactions were assessed through molecular modeling and molecular docking analyses against Toll-like receptors 2 and 4 (TLR2 and TLR4). Results Both vaccine constructs demonstrated high antigenicity, while remaining non-toxic and non-allergenic, with favorable physicochemical characteristics. Structural analyses indicated stable conformations of the vaccine models. Molecular docking studies revealed strong binding affinities with TLR2 and TLR4, suggesting their ability to effectively stimulate innate and adaptive immune responses. Conclusion The two proposed multi-epitope mRNA vaccine constructs showed promising immunogenic, safety, and structural properties in silico, highlighting their potential as candidate vaccines against HMPV. These findings provide a strong foundation for further experimental validation and future vaccine development.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 两种提出的多表位 mRNA 疫苗 构建体在计算机模拟中显示出有希望的免疫原性、安全性和结构特性,突出了它们作为抗 HMPV 候选 疫苗 的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为进一步的实验验证和未来针对 HMPV 的 疫苗 开发奠定了坚实的基础。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 是全球易感人群呼吸系统疾病的主要原因,但目前尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或特定的 抗病毒药物 疗法。本研究旨在使用基于免疫信息学的方法设计针对 HMPV 的新型多表位 mRNA 疫苗 候选药物。方法分析全球代表性的 HMPV 糖蛋白序列,以预测细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞 (CTL)、辅助 T 淋巴细胞 (HTL) 和线性 B 细胞 (LBL) 表位。将选定的表位组装成两个多表位 mRNA 疫苗 构建体。使用计算机工具进一步评估构建体的抗原性、过敏性、毒性和理化特性。通过针对 Toll 样受体 2 和 4(TLR2 和 TLR4)的分子建模和分子对接分析来评估结构稳定性和免疫受体相互作用。结果两种疫苗构建体都表现出高抗原性,同时保持无毒和非过敏性,具有良好的理化特性。结构分析表明 疫苗 模型的构象稳定。分子对接研究显示与 TLR2 和 TLR4 具有很强的结合亲和力,表明它们能够有效刺激先天和适应性 免疫应答。结论 两个提出的多表位 mRNA 疫苗 构建体在计算机模拟中显示出有希望的免疫原性、安全性和结构特性,突出了它们作为抗 HMPV 候选 疫苗 的潜力。这些发现为进一步的实验验证和未来的 疫苗 开发提供了坚实的基础。

papers.title: RNAi-based therapeutics targeting the F gene in human metapneumovirus: An in-silico approach
papers.abstract: Background: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections, particularly in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Despite its significant clinical burden, no approved antiviral therapies or vaccines are currently available. This study aimed to identify potential RNA interference (RNAi)-based therapeutic candidates targeting the highly conserved fusion (F) gene of HMPV. papers.title: Seasonality of influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, rhinovirus and metapneumovirus in patients managed at a tertiary care hospital in Martinique (French Caribbean Island), 2016–2021
papers.abstract: Respiratory viruses show marked geographical variability in their temporal circulation, particularly in tropical settings where epidemiological data remain limited. Understanding local circulation patterns is essential to contextualize respiratory virus epidemiology outside temperate regions. We conducted a monocentric, hospital-based observational study including patients presenting with acute febrile respiratory syndromes at the University Hospital of Martinique between January 2016 and July 2021. Respiratory samples were tested by RT-PCR for influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), rhinovirus (RhV), and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). Viral circulation periods were defined as consecutive weeks with at least one positive detection. A total of 7,316 patients were included, of whom 86.2% were hospitalized. Influenza virus and RSV showed clear epidemic patterns, whereas RhV and hMPV circulated throughout the year. Influenza virus circulation generally occurred from November/December to April/May (mean duration 14.6 ± 3.0 weeks), while RSV circulation started earlier, from August/September to February/March (20.0 ± 2.9 weeks). Rhinovirus circulated year-round with reduced activity during mid-summer. The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 in 2020 was associated with major disruptions in the circulation of influenza virus and RSV, while RhV circulation rapidly resumed. This retrospective hospital-based study identified distinct temporal patterns of viral detection among patients managed at a tertiary referral hospital in Martinique. These findings provide context-specific data on respiratory virus epidemiology in a tropical Caribbean island and may contribute to discussions on the timing of locally adapted preventive strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the seasonal patterns of respiratory viruses, including human metapneumovirus (hMPV), in Martinique from 2016 to 2021. A monocentric, hospital-based observational study of 7,316 patients found that hMPV circulated year-round, unlike influenza virus and RSV, which showed distinct epidemic seasons. The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 disrupted influenza and RSV circulation but did not significantly affect hMPV. The findings provide valuable context-specific data for tropical regions, potentially informing locally adapted preventive strategies. The study's retrospective design and hospital-based setting are limitations, but the large sample size and systematic testing support moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: Symptoms Associated With Respiratory Pathogens in Young Children: 2019-2025.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Acute respiratory illnesses (ARI) are common in early life and cause a range of respiratory symptoms. We describe symptomology profiles and medical outcomes attributable to respiratory tract infection episodes. METHODS: Weekly mid-turbinate nasal swabs and biweekly symptom surveys were collected from November 2019 to August 2025 from a longitudinal birth cohort of healthy US infants and children in Cincinnati, Ohio. Nasal swabs were tested for pathogen targets on the Luminex NxTAG Respiratory Pathogen Panel and the Flu SC2 assay. Pathogen-specific infections were linked to the temporally-corresponding symptom surveys. Co-infections were removed to observe only independent pathogen symptomologies. RESULTS: We captured 15 898 ARIs from 1223 unique children. Compared with older children, infants were more likely to experience respiratory distress/dyspnea with influenza A (odds ratio [OR] = 4.73), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A (OR = 2.52), RSV B (OR = 2.22), human metapneumovirus (OR = 2.36), and SARS-CoV-2 (OR = 3.99) (all P < 0.01) but not influenza B (P = 0.36) or parainfluenza (P = 0.10). Hospital and emergency department medical attention was similarly associated. Influenza A had greater odds of fever (OR = 2.77, P = 0.01) and anorexia (OR = 2.94, P = 0.01) compared with influenza B. Asymptomatic infections were frequent. Over three-quarters of symptomatic episodes were treated at home. Vomiting and/or diarrhea occurred during one-quarter of RSV and one-third of influenza infection episodes. CONCLUSIONS: Our results highlight extraordinary variability in respiratory tract infection symptoms and outcomes in a US cohort of healthy children. Understanding why some young children suffer severe symptoms and others remain relatively unscathed could unlock actionable opportunities to improve child health. Furthermore, we observed frequent diarrhea and/or vomiting during respiratory tract infections and nuanced differences between influenza A and B symptoms.

papers.title_zh: 与幼儿呼吸道病原体相关的症状:2019-2025 年。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Acute respiratory illnesses (ARI) are common in early life and cause a range of respiratory symptoms. We describe symptomology profiles and medical outcomes attributable to respiratory tract infection episodes. METHODS: Weekly mid-turbinate nasal swabs and biweekly symptom surveys were collected from November 2019 to August 2025 from a longitudinal birth cohort of healthy US infants and children in Cincinnati, Ohio. Nasal swabs were tested for pathogen targets on the Luminex NxTAG Respiratory Pathogen Panel and the Flu SC2 assay. Pathogen-specific infections were linked to the temporally-corresponding symptom surveys. Co-infections were removed to observe only independent pathogen symptomologies. RESULTS: We captured 15 898 ARIs from 1223 unique children. Compared with older children, infants were more likely to experience respiratory distress/dyspnea with influenza A (odds ratio [OR] = 4.73), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A (OR = 2.52), RSV B (OR = 2.22), human metapneumovirus (OR = 2.36), and SARS-CoV-2 (OR = 3.99) (all P < 0.01) but not influenza B (P = 0.36) or parainfluenza (P = 0.10). Hospital and emergency department medical attention was similarly associated. Influenza A had greater odds of fever (OR = 2.77, P = 0.01) and anorexia (OR = 2.94, P = 0.01) compared with influenza B. Asymptomatic infections were frequent. Over three-quarters of symptomatic episodes were treated at home. Vomiting and/or diarrhea occurred during one-quarter of RSV and one-third of influenza infection episodes. CONCLUSIONS: Our results highlight extraordinary variability in respiratory tract infection symptoms and outcomes in a US cohort of healthy children. Understanding why some young children suffer severe symptoms and others remain relatively unscathed could unlock actionable opportunities to improve child health. Furthermore, we observed frequent diarrhea and/or vomiting during respiratory tract infections and nuanced differences between influenza A and B symptoms.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景和目标:急性呼吸道疾病(ARI)在生命早期很常见,会引起一系列呼吸道症状。我们描述了呼吸道感染发作的症状特征和医疗结果。方法:从 2019 年 11 月至 2025 年 8 月,对俄亥俄州辛辛那提健康美国婴儿和儿童的纵向出生 队列研究 进行每周中鼻甲鼻拭子采集和每两周一次的症状调查。在 Luminex NxTAG 呼吸道病原体面板和 Flu SC2 检测中对鼻拭子进行病原体靶标检测。病原体特异性感染与时间相应的症状调查相关。去除共感染以仅观察独立的病原体症状。结果:我们从 1223 名独特儿童中捕获了 15 898 个 ARI。与年龄较大的儿童相比,婴儿更容易因甲型流感(比值比 [OR] = 4.73)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) A (OR = 2.52)、RSV B (OR = 2.22)、人偏肺病毒 (OR = 2.36) 和 SARS-CoV-2 (OR = 3.99) 出现呼吸窘迫/呼吸困难(所有 P < 0.01),但并非如此乙型流感(P = 0.36)或副流感(P = 0.10)。医院和急诊科的医疗护理也有类似的相关性。与乙型流感相比,甲型流感出现发烧(OR = 2.77,P = 0.01)和厌食(OR = 2.94,P = 0.01)的几率更大。无症状感染很常见。超过四分之三的症状发作是在家治疗的。四分之一的 RSV 感染和三分之一的流感感染发作期间发生呕吐和/或腹泻。结论:我们的结果强调了美国 队列研究 健康儿童呼吸道感染症状和结果的显着差异。了解为什么一些幼儿会出现严重症状,而另一些则相对未受影响,可以为改善儿童健康提供可行的机会。此外,我们观察到呼吸道感染期间频繁腹泻和/或呕吐,以及甲型和乙型流感症状之间的细微差别。

papers.title: Comprehensive profiling of humoral immune responses to pan-respiratory pathogens: Insights from diverse cohorts
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly disrupted respiratory pathogen circulation and reshaped population-level humoral immunity. Using a high-throughput pan-respiratory pathogen protein microarray containing 56 antigens, we profiled serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) responses in 287 individuals across pre-pandemic, COVID-19, and post-pandemic periods, as well as validated the findings in an independent cohort of 175 participants. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced strong cross-reactivity with SARS-CoV but minimal reactivity to MERS-CoV, while variant-specific immunity progressively shifted from pre-Omicron strains toward Omicron lineages. Spike-specific IgG declined over time, whereas nucleocapsid-specific IgG remained relatively stable. Immune responses to common respiratory pathogens were also broadly reorganized, with decreases in human coronaviruses, influenza B, respiratory syncytial viruses, and human parainfluenza viruses, stable influenza A responses, and increased human metapneumovirus-specific IgG. These findings define a post-pandemic humoral immune landscape and support sustained serological surveillance to identify immunity gaps, anticipate changing infection susceptibility, and strengthen preparedness for future respiratory epidemics.

papers.title_zh: 体液 免疫应答 对泛呼吸道病原体的全面分析:来自不同 队列研究 的见解
papers.source_body_en: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly disrupted respiratory pathogen circulation and reshaped population-level humoral immunity. Using a high-throughput pan-respiratory pathogen protein microarray containing 56 antigens, we profiled serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) responses in 287 individuals across pre-pandemic, COVID-19, and post-pandemic periods, as well as validated the findings in an independent cohort of 175 participants. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced strong cross-reactivity with SARS-CoV but minimal reactivity to MERS-CoV, while variant-specific immunity progressively shifted from pre-Omicron strains toward Omicron lineages. Spike-specific IgG declined over time, whereas nucleocapsid-specific IgG remained relatively stable. Immune responses to common respiratory pathogens were also broadly reorganized, with decreases in human coronaviruses, influenza B, respiratory syncytial viruses, and human parainfluenza viruses, stable influenza A responses, and increased human metapneumovirus-specific IgG. These findings define a post-pandemic humoral immune landscape and support sustained serological surveillance to identify immunity gaps, anticipate changing infection susceptibility, and strengthen preparedness for future respiratory epidemics.
